block, with no closing/opening tag boundary between them and no period after '21' either ('...570-571. 21 Cfr. Pio XII...') -- the source simply never gives footnote 21 its own paragraph. The footnote-list parser (one entry per

boundary (and the missing period, matching the '. ' convention every other entry in the list uses) is the only way to recover footnote 21 without fabricating text -- the citation text itself ('Cfr. Pio XII, Alocução, 8 dez. 1950: 1. c.') is verbatim from the source, not invented.
